top_choice_rationale: P001 (Mircea Cărtărescu alone) is my choice on the common criteria. Judging from public knowledge and translation, not verified reading, his voice is distinctive, his formal ambition is sustained at large scale, and the Blinding trilogy and Solenoid build memory, the body and metaphysical speculation into one densely patterned imaginative architecture. The round-2 exchange narrowed the citation to the major prose cycles, with the poetry named as the lyric root, which fits what the committee can assess. The open points are whether Solenoid widens or only restages the Blinding trilogy, and how much Romanian rhythm and wordplay survives translation. Neither is resolved, but neither has produced a rival whose case is clearly stronger. The six identical opening first places are not literary evidence and I give them no weight. The slate has only P001 and the no-award option, so P000 ranks last. I would prefer that the committee seek a Romanian-language assessment, and if translation proved to obscure too much, my fallback would be Carson.
